title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
gist: Microsoft shipped a public-preview local CLI (the Azure CLI logicapp extension) for Azure Logic Apps Standard that lets workflows be created, run, validated and tested without VS Code; MVPs frame it as deliberately designed for AI coding agents needing a deterministic validate-run-test loop, while caveats note local runs can still touch live Azure resources.

themes.theme: Logic Apps CLI scope and mechanics

insights.claim: Microsoft's public-preview logicapp extension for the Azure CLI adds 19 command groups with 64 commands for Azure Logic Apps Standard, alongside thirteen existing cloud-management commands it leaves untouched, and requires Azure CLI 2.67.0 or later.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Signals Microsoft investing in CLI-first (agent-friendly) surfaces for its integration/low-code platform.
insights.locator: The extension installs automatically the first

insights.claim: The Azure Logic Apps Standard CLI provides offline workflow validation by default and a local runtime host on port 7071 that launches the Azurite storage emulator when configured for development storage, enabling workflows to run without Visual Studio Code.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Reduces dependence on the IDE designer, broadening automation and CI use of Logic Apps.
insights.locator: The extension installs automatically the first

insights.claim: The Logic Apps CLI's runtime doctor command is strictly read-only and test execution is split into create, plan and run steps, with only test run actually building and executing tests under a deadline.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Read-only diagnostics and staged execution are design patterns that make tools safe for autonomous agents.
insights.quote: never installs, downloads, starts, stops, repairs, decrypts settings, changes context, or contacts cloud storage
insights.locator: The doctor and test commands say

insights.claim: Microsoft MVP Sagar Sharma argues the Logic Apps CLI is deliberately designed for AI-assisted coding: an agent validates, runs, inspects and tests in a loop until green, with secrets passed through stdin rather than the command line.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Vendor tooling is being re-architected around agent loops; deterministic validation surfaces become a competitive feature.
insights.quote: literally pitched as adding determinism to local AI-assisted coding

insights.claim: Sagar Sharma contends that an AI agent without a deterministic way to validate and run a workflow is effectively guessing, which is why he called the Logic Apps CLI the sleeper hit of Microsoft's recent Logic Apps announcements.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agent productivity depends on deterministic feedback tooling, an investable layer in dev tooling.

insights.claim: Microsoft MVP Sonny Gillissen claims the Logic Apps CLI lets a new hire get a local runtime up in minutes instead of hours and lets integration flows be tested from CI/CD pipelines instead of by hand.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Faster onboarding and pipeline testing lower the cost of operating Azure integration estates.
insights.locator: Sonny Gillissen, also a Microsoft MVP

insights.claim: Christos Panagiotidis cautions that Microsoft's own Logic Apps CLI walkthrough uses live Azure and Microsoft 365 resources and some commands change deployed connections, so a 'local' run can have remote effects.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agent-driven 'local' tooling can still mutate production cloud state — a governance risk.
insights.locator: That passing remark is the one

insights.claim: Microsoft states that Logic Apps CLI validation does not establish authorization or business correctness, and the extension's pull request concedes that native SDK test code is trusted rather than sandboxed and that Linux CI results prove neither native SDK execution nor execution against live Azure.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Green CI on agent-written workflows is not proof of correctness; security exposure from unsandboxed tests.
insights.quote: does not establish authorization or business correctness

insights.claim: Azure CLI extensions do not update with the CLI itself, so reproducible comparisons of Logic Apps CLI results require recording CLI, extension, runtime and project versions alongside each result.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Version drift is an operational hazard for agent-driven pipelines.

insights.claim: The Logic Apps CLI preview cannot change the state of a running local app and edits workflow.json directly, so the visual designer remains in VS Code until Microsoft ships the broader command surface it says will follow soon; the agent bootstrap command does not exist yet.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Feature gap means the agent-first workflow is still incomplete; watch for the follow-on release.
insights.locator: Microsoft has said a broader command
